messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a consistent NDCG dip (~0.02) on the new reranker when evaling the url/html-heavy slice. Seems correlated with queries that include long raw URLs or embedded HTML snippets.

sachin: hmm that's a decent gap. Is this in float32 or the int8 bring-up?

julia: which dataset slice exactly? user-search logs or curated benchmark?

maria: user-search logs slice 'url_html_heavy' (we've been using a regex to pick queries with >2 'http' or '<a>' tags). Baseline (r2a-fp32) NDCG@10=0.412, new model (r3a-quant) NDCG@10=0.391. MRR also drops but smaller.

eval-bot: quick reminder — evaluation harness used: https://ci.redwood/internal/eval/run/789 (seed=42, topk=10, trunc=1024)

sachin: two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenizer/byte-level differences handling punctuation in URLs, 2) model learned to overweight domain tokens and mis-rank snippets.

julia: we should try simple preproc ablations: strip HTML tags, normalize urls to <URL>, and test candidate truncation at 256 chars vs 1024. Even upstream tokenization parity can matter.

maria: agreed. I ran a quick smoke today:
```
# smoke commands
python -m eval.run --slice url_html_heavy --model r3a-fp32 --preproc "strip_html" --topk 10
python -m eval.run --slice url_html_heavy --model r3a-quant --preproc "url_norm" --topk 10
```
Outputs: r3a-fp32 (strip_html) NDCG@10=0.409, r3a-quant (url_norm) NDCG@10=0.404. Both better than raw but still below baseline.

sam: good signal. Did you try normalizing to the same tokenizer input? small mismatch in whitespace can shift tokenization.

maria: not yet. Next step: run tokenizer parity check with the production tokenizer binary and our eval tokenizer. I suspect URL percent-encoding makes token sequence longer causing kv-cache misalignment in quant path.

sachin: also try candidate-side normalization. If docs have full HTML payloads, the reranker might be focusing on anchor text vs surrounding context. Candidate truncation could push anchors out of window.

julia: propose an experiment matrix:
- preproc: [raw, strip_html, url_norm, strip_html+url_norm]
- candidate_trunc: [256, 512, 1024]
- model: [r2a-fp32 (baseline), r3a-fp32, r3a-quant]
Run on url_html_heavy and a control slice (short-queries) so we can diff.

maria: timeline: I'll kick off a small grid tomorrow with sampling (n=10k) and post results. Can someone add a quick eval job to the job queue with higher priority? tag @eng-ml-runner?

eval-bot: scheduled job 7721 in cluster-high-prio queue. ETA ~3h. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/jobs/7721

sachin: after we get metrics, let's also export top-5 predictions for a random 200 queries and eyeball failures — sometimes it's just a regex edgecase.

maria: yes. If preproc fixes >60% of gap we can bake normalization into the onboarding template. If not, we'll need to dig into model attention diagnostics and possibly change candidate pooling.

julia: also keep an eye on token-efficiency: url_norm reduces token count which helps latency/cost — win if quality holds.

sam: noted. I can help with the eyeball pass and candidate-side normalizer.

maria: thanks. I'll post the job results + a short CSV with metrics and a gist of 200 failure cases when ready :thumbsup:
